description: The console window: core APIs, autostart, clipboard. No window-state grant: Rust drives that plugin, and a page call to `restoreStateCurrent()` would bring back a saved `decorated: true` (v0.4.0 note §3, B1). The folder picker is `rfd` called from an app command, not a plugin, so it needs no permission here. NO UPDATER PERMISSION IS GRANTED (R-P4a-30): the app drives `tauri-plugin-updater` from Rust, through `Manager::state` (`updater_builder`/`updater`), which is not capability-gated at all — the only thing `updater:default` would add is the plugin's four IPC commands, and `updater:allow-install` / `updater:allow-download-and-install` would let any page script call `invoke('plugin:updater|download_and_install')` and walk straight past `update_offer`'s mid-run gate and `hold_for_install`. The gate lives in `check_for_updates` and `install_update`, and those are the only doors the page gets. The five `core:window` grants are the frameless window's drawn chrome (minimize, maximize/restore, close, drag, theme); there is no `allow-show`, because Rust shows the window.
